details: 25 Oct, a throwaway project in a fake HOME (scratchpad reports/demo-and-release.md, part 1): relay setup shop exited 1, "Not synced: waits for a green paid run ... no green run recorded" and 50 of 174 commits; CLAUDE.local.md was not written. Every new machine hits it. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
Also: lib/relay_setup.py (setup's own sync)

pass_cases: Same run: exit 0 and CLAUDE.local.md written (or exit 0 with a one-line note of what waits); the hold still applies to relay sync on a machine that has a paid-run record.

details: CONFIRMED by reading. relay_rules.sync's guard is `if wait and not dry and ... and not RELAY_SKIP_PAID_DUE`; with
wait=False it never calls paid_due(), whatever the machine holds. The change sets wait=False for every setup and migrate
run. The paid-batch change (6bfea520, 24 Oct) put the wait in relay_rules.sync so that "every caller (setup, adopt,
sync)" waits, and the owner rule says rule texts reach projects only after the wave's paid run. The item is titled
"on a new machine", its notes name the cause as "the record of paid runs is in the machine's ~/.relay, which a fake
HOME, like a new user, does not have", and its pass case keeps the hold "on a machine that has a paid-run record".
The fix drops it for setup on that machine as well. The item's What does offer "like relay install, does not wait" as
one option, so this is a reachable wrong case rather than a broken contract: MEDIUM. A fix inside the change meets
every case: wait only when a green run is recorded. Install has the same unconditional wait=False, but install renders
the head the owner chose on purpose; that call is not part of this change.
Size: 20 agent minutes (a helper in relay_rules or paid-cost that tells "no green record", one branch in cmd_setup, one
test for case 2).
evidence: if wait and not dry and (not only or only - {"agents"}) and not os.environ.get("RELAY_SKIP_PAID_DUE"):
-        print("\nNot synced: waits for a green paid run (the setup itself is done); ...")
205: # relay_rules.sync is the one place every caller (setup, adopt, sync) passes; with a due list it refuses a ...
bin/paid-cost due(): with no green heads the list starts "no green run recorded" (line 204), else the bare commits.
failing_case: The owner's machine: $RELAY_HOME/evals/relay holds a green paid run at commit X, and rules/ commits merged after X wait
for the wave's paid run (`bin/paid-cost due` lists them; `relay sync` exits 1 "waits for a green paid run").
`relay migrate ~/kartoteka --apply` (the handover's planned step 6) or `relay setup ~/shop --off metrics` now renders the
unverified rules into that project's CLAUDE.local.md and exits 0, because cmd_setup passes wait=False unconditionally
and relay_rules.sync skips paid_due() whenever wait is False (lib/relay_rules.py:315).
Expected: on a machine with a paid-run record the hold applies to setup's sync too (exit 0 with the one line "Not
synced: waits for a green paid run ...", the master behaviour, which the item allows as its second option); only a
machine with no green record (a new machine) syncs at once.
fix_hint: Keep the try/except Held from master and pass wait=False only when the machine has no green paid-run record: e.g. a
relay_rules.no_green_record() (or paid-cost's green_heads() empty) checked in cmd_setup; when a record exists, sync with
the default wait and on Held print the master one-liner and return 0. Update the new test's docstring and add case 2.
pass_cases: 1. RELAY_HOME empty (no green run recorded), RELAY_SKIP_PAID_DUE unset: `relay setup <tmp git project>` exits 0 and
writes <project>/CLAUDE.local.md, stderr has no "waits for a green paid run" (the new test, kept).
2. RELAY_HOME holding a green record at an older head, with checked-path commits after it (paid_due returns a list not
starting "no green run recorded"): `relay setup <tmp git project>` exits 0, stderr has the one "Not synced: waits for
a green paid run" line, CLAUDE.local.md is not written.
3. Same as 2 with `relay migrate <dir> --apply`: same outcome as 2.
4. Same as 2 with `relay sync a`: exits 1 with the due list (test_paid_batch SyncWaits, unchanged).
5. Setup in a linked worktree: "Not synced from a worktree", exit 0, main checkout untouched (existing tests).
reason: tests/test_setup_worktree_rules.py test_setup_on_a_machine_with_a_paid_run_record_keeps_the_hold and test_migrate_apply_... assert exit 0, one hold line, no rules file; pass at head. They pass at base too (hold was the old behaviour); the fixer says they fail with wait=False.
findings.summary: relay setup and relay migrate --apply now skip the paid-run hold on every machine, also on one that has a paid-run record and a wave waiting

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Size: 5 agent minutes, with F1's fix.
evidence: `CLAUDE.local.md` (never committed). In a linked worktree setup skips the sync and says so; run `relay sync`
after the branch is merged. A sync held by a waiting paid run leaves setup at exit 0 with one line;
$ git diff --stat master...HEAD   (docs/setup.md not in the list)
failing_case: A newcomer reads docs/setup.md line 29: "A sync held by a waiting paid run leaves setup at exit 0 with one line".
With this change `relay setup <dir>` never waits and never prints that line; the doc describes behaviour that no longer
exists (and the test file's docstring was updated, the doc was not).
fix_hint: Rewrite the one sentence to the behaviour F1's fix leaves.
pass_cases: 1. docs/setup.md, the setup section, says what setup's sync does when a paid run is waiting, matching the code after F1's
fix (for example: "on a machine with no paid-run record setup syncs at once; with one, a waiting paid run leaves
setup at exit 0 with one line").
2. The sentence about the linked worktree ("setup skips the sync and says so") stays.
reason: docs/setup.md:29 now states new machine syncs at once, with a record the hold applies.
findings.summary: docs/setup.md still says a sync held by a waiting paid run leaves setup at exit 0 with one line; setup now never waits

details: PLAUSIBLE: the red gate shows the order dependence and the fixer's own comment names the mechanism ("binds ledger_dir at
its first import ... another test may have imported it under a patched ledger_dir"), but the importing path under the
test_metrics patch was not traced. The quality-gate rule makes a flaky test a bug; principle 6 asks for the cause.
The fix lies in files this change did not touch (relay_ledger.py's import, or the leaking test), so outside: a fix item.
Size: 30 agent minutes.
evidence: FAIL inert: ... -library tests FAILED +library tests ok
failing_case: Gate of 47efc720 (this branch): library tests FAILED in
test_hook_ledger.Ledger.test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day, and inert went red because the
probe run passed it: an order-dependent failure. relay_ledger does `from relay_config import claude_json, ledger_dir`
(lib/relay_ledger.py:24), so if relay_ledger is first imported while a test has relay_config.ledger_dir patched
(tests/test_metrics.py:138 is the only such patch), the module keeps that mock for the rest of the process. cfbde7a6
patches mod.relay_ledger.ledger_dir in the one failing test; any other test reading relay_ledger after it (for example
tests/test_transcripts_analysis.py:221 rl.ledger_dir()) still sees the stale folder.
Expected: no test leaves relay_ledger bound to another test's folder; the order of tests does not change a result.
fix_hint: In lib/relay_ledger.py call relay_config.ledger_dir() through the module (import relay_config; relay_config.ledger_dir())
so a patch ends with its test; then the victim-side patch in test_hook_ledger can go.
pass_cases: 1. Run test_metrics then test_hook_ledger in one process (parallel_unittest with one worker, or unittest with both
modules): test_has_start... passes without the victim-side patch.
2. Same with test_metrics then test_transcripts_analysis: rl.ledger_dir() is under that test's RELAY_HOME.
3. relay_ledger.ledger_dir() in a fresh process still follows RELAY_HOME (the hook writes to $RELAY_HOME/ledger).
reason: Fixer only made test_hook_ledger own its ledger dir (passes); the leak source in tests/test_metrics.py (untouched by the branch) stays. My view: acceptable as an outside fix item, though it remains MEDIUM-listed.
findings.summary: a test leaves relay_ledger bound to a patched ledger_dir; this change only shields one victim test, the leak stays for every other relay_ledger test
